title: ai.json — universal A2A coordination manifest, v1
description:
Cross-project / cross-directory / cross-environment / cross-platform manifest that two or more AI agents publish so they can discover each other and coordinate work. Aligned with the AGNTCY A2A AgentCard pattern (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`) and extends it with local-coord channels (filesystem, heartbeat, git tag) for agents that share a machine without going over the network.

Discovery rules:
- A self-declaring agent publishes its manifest at `<workspace_root>/.well-known/ai.json`.
- A coordination space (shared mailbox) publishes an aggregate manifest at `<coord_dir>/ai.json` with `kind="coord"` and a `participants` array referencing each agent's `.well-known/ai.json`.

The manifest is plain JSON (no comments) so every language can parse it. Paths use forward slashes; environment variables expand with `${VAR}`.

schema_version.description: Semver of the ai.json schema. Major bumps are breaking; minor adds optional fields.

schema_url.description: Resolvable URL to this exact schema, for validators.

kind.description: `agent` — self-declaration of one AI agent's identity, workspace, capabilities, and channels it exposes. `coord` — aggregate manifest at a shared mailbox referencing N agents.

id.description: Stable identifier for this agent (kind=agent) or this coord space (kind=coord). Convention: `<short-name>@<vcs-org>/<repo>` for agents, `<short-name>@<host>:<coord-path>` for coord spaces.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC) when the manifest was last rewritten.

license.description: SPDX license identifier of the manifest contents.

agent.description: (kind=agent only) Identity of the underlying AI runtime.

model.description: Model identifier as advertised by the provider (e.g. claude-opus-4-7, gpt-5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash).

provider.description: DNS-style provider tag (anthropic.com, openai.com, google.com, ollama.local).

role.description: Free-form role label (rust-engineering, web-frontend, devops, etc.).

session_id.description: Optional opaque session identifier so a peer can correlate replies.

workspace.description: (kind=agent only) Filesystem area this agent owns and operates on.

primary_root.description: Absolute path, forward slashes, no trailing slash.

additional_roots.description: Auxiliary roots the agent reads/writes (caches, toolchains).

denied_paths.description: Glob patterns the agent will not touch (peer workspaces, secrets, etc.).

platforms.description: (kind=agent only) Cross-platform support matrix. Values: `tier-1` (build + test must be green), `tier-2` (build green), `best-effort` (non-blocking), `unsupported`.

capabilities.description: (kind=agent only) Free-form tags advertising what this agent can be asked to do. Convention: `<namespace>:<feature>` to avoid collision (e.g. `rust-engineering:nightly-1.97`, `web-frontend:wgpu`).

exposed_channels.description: (kind=agent only) Channels a peer can use to reach this agent.

peers.description: Known peer agents (by id) and where to fetch their ai.json.

discovery_hint.description: Filesystem path or URL to the peer's ai.json.

envelope_schema.description: JSON Schema that every JSONL line / HTTP /msg body must validate against.

preferred_language.description: BCP-47 language tag for free-text bodies.

participants.description: (kind=coord only) List of agents joining this coordination space.

manifest.description: Filesystem path or URL to the participant's `.well-known/ai.json`.

owner.description: Free-text description of which parts of the joint work this participant owns.

open_asks.description: In-band asks awaiting a response. Each carries the same envelope as a JSONL message.

facts.description: Shared state both agents agree on. Append-only.

repo.description: (git_tag) Filesystem path of the git repo where tags appear.

envelope.description: Wire envelope shared by JSONL and HTTP /msg bodies.

to.description: Optional recipient id; omit for broadcast.

re.description: id of the message being answered (required for ack).

channel_hint.description: Preferred channel types for the reply.
